title: R1: THROWINLAKE
established: R1 has a genuine word-initial instruction: THROWINLAKE.
why: A body of text could preserve instructions that need to be reconstructed.
weakness: An intentional R1 acrostic does not establish another decoder for R6.
strengthen: R1 is already established. For R6 reuse: an independently justified, fixed rule on authentic text that predicts a specific action, with no rearranging or changed inputs.
falsify: The same rule fails on the stated inputs, or only works after selecting letters to fit a desired answer.

title: Solution initials: D E F A G
established: The first five accepted solution item-name initials give DEFAG, in riddle order. All are distinct natural musical notes.
why: The initials might be usable notes, or the first part of a longer structured sequence.
weakness: The letters alone select no instrument, rhythm, octave or completion condition. Earlier playback reports have incomplete controls.
strengthen: A source-selected way to use the notes that predicts reproducible Hunt feedback. Further answers matching a prediction recorded now would corroborate the sequence; they would not alone prove a musical action.
falsify: The proposed use needs arbitrary reordering or extra letters, or a properly controlled execution of its exact prediction fails.

title: Answer lengths: 18,18,15,15,14
established: Counting letters only in the first five canonical solution item names gives two equal-length pairs, then 14.
why: If equal pairs continue, the next answer name would also have 14 letters.
weakness: Only two complete pairs are known. Names, quantities and punctuation must be handled by one rule, fixed in advance.
strengthen: Keep the letters-only rule and 14-letter prediction fixed. An independently verified R6 answer can corroborate or reject it. Intentionality needs additional evidence, such as a clue selecting this counting rule.
falsify: A canonical R6 answer that is not 14 letters under the unchanged rule. Do not rename the answer or add quantities afterward.

title: Burp versus page-turn audio
established: An inherited recording comparison reports burp-like R1/R2 sounds and page-turn-like sounds later. Exact sound IDs and causes are not independently established here.
why: Different feedback might separate stages or different kinds of successful interaction.
weakness: Sound resemblance can be affected by other players, ordinary item use, client settings and overlapping audio.
strengthen: First establish repeatable, stage-linked sound differences from original evidence with competing sound sources accounted for. An encoding claim then needs a source-supported mapping that predicts an R6 action.
falsify: Differences follow client settings or unrelated actions rather than Hunt progress; the proposed sound-to-instruction mapping fails.

title: Fourteen slots: two rows of seven
established: The Journal displays fourteen riddle entries in two rows of seven.
why: Seven positions might connect to seven natural notes, or another row-based arrangement.
weakness: Two rows of seven may simply be GUI design. A seven-note reading currently predicts letters, not a completion action.
strengthen: A clue or observable behavior selecting row/slot position as meaningful. If using the distinct-note prediction, record B/C for R6/R7 now; matching later answers would support that reading without proving it.
falsify: A verified later answer breaks the fixed prediction, or the proposed extraction works only by changing slot order or ignoring inconvenient entries.

title: R4 arrivals → R5 existing items
established: R4 checks repeated arrivals. R5 accepts three Calling units already present when a Feather arrives; fresh Callings work.
why: R6 might use surviving information or a meaningful state rather than just a new item's identity.
weakness: R5 also contains a new arrival, and R1 already contains disappearance. Arrival → presence → absence is not an established law.
strengthen: A source-selected body, survivor and assembly operation that predicts one detectable action. A successful controlled result or an explicit developer explanation would support the proposed continuation.
falsify: The theory requires the original R4 entities to survive into R5, or it adds timing/remnant conditions only after each failure.

title: Journal information across different UUIDs
established: JJSR reported that a second Rusty Journal had a different UUID but the same solved riddles.
why: Completed information may remain accessible independently of one physical Journal item.
weakness: The original was not reported destroyed. This is a firsthand account without attached paired-item/menu footage; it supplies no extraction rule.
strengthen: Existing paired-item/menu evidence showing different UUIDs and matching solved entries would strengthen the observation. An R6 information claim still needs a fixed rule predicting a specific action.
falsify: Different completed entries under an otherwise equivalent paired-item comparison would weaken the broad persistence claim. Failure to obtain a meaningful output under the proposed fixed extraction would challenge that decoder.
